steps.text: Hi Alex, I'm Remy — your care guide. How did your visit with Dr. Lee go? I hope you're feeling okay. Your records were just updated, so let's turn today's visit into a simple plan.
I'll have Jack pull your latest records, and Jill will be right here to answer anything you want to understand.

thoughts: Ready to explain anything in plain language…

steps.text: Got it — here's what's new since your visit. Your A1c and lipid results just posted, your metformin prescription was sent to your pharmacy, and a diabetic eye-exam referral is pending. One thing stood out: your fasting glucose has been climbing — 102 in 2024, 110 last year, and 152 now.
Let's make sense of what the doctor told you. Go ahead and ask me anything about your visit — just hold the talk button and speak.
My doctor said my sugar is just a little high and to watch my diet. But my A1c is 7.8 — is that actually diabetes? And do I really need to take metformin?

I hear you — it's confusing when it's framed as 'just a little high.' Here's the straight answer: your HbA1c is 7.8%, and anything at or above 6.5% meets the definition of diabetes. So yes, this is type 2 diabetes — not just borderline. Your A1c is a three-month average of your blood sugar. The good news: 7.8% is very treatable. Metformin is the standard first medication — it helps your body use insulin better, it's inexpensive, and most people tolerate it well, especially with food. It's worth starting, and you can always revisit the plan with Dr. Lee at your follow-up.
Here's your plan for the next few weeks — and I'll take care of the busywork right now.
Your metformin is ready for pickup at 4 PM at the CVS on Main Street — I've sent directions to your phone.
